publications.title: A Large Language Model-Powered Map of Metabolomics Research
publications.subtitle: bioRxiv
publications.description: We present a comprehensive map of the metabolomics research landscape, synthesizing insights from over 80,000 publications. Using PubMedBERT, we transformed abstracts into 768-dimensional embeddings that capture the nuanced thematic structure of the field. Dimensionality reduction with t-SNE revealed distinct clusters corresponding to key domains such as analytical chemistry, plant biology, pharmacology, and clinical diagnostics. In addition, a neural topic modeling pipeline refined with GPT-4o mini reclassified the corpus into 20 distinct topics-ranging from "Plant Stress Response Mechanisms" and "NMR Spectroscopy Innovations" to "COVID-19 Metabolomic and Immune Responses." Temporal analyses further highlight trends including the rise of deep learning methods post-2015 and a continued focus on biomarker discovery. Integration of metadata such as publication statistics and sample sizes provide additional context to these evolving research dynamics. An interactive web application (https://metascape.streamlit.app/) enables dynamic exploration of these insights. Overall, this study offers a robust framework for literature synthesis that empowers researchers, clinicians, and policymakers to identify emerging research trajectories and address critical challenges in metabolomics, while also sharing our perspectives on key trends shaping the field.

publications.title: IE-GADCI: An End-to-End Incoherence-Enhanced Generative Adversarial Deep Compressive Imaging
publications.subtitle: IEEE
publications.description: In this work, we present a new computational framework designed to jointly optimize both the illumination pattern and the image reconstruction algorithm for block-scanning SPI, under the principle of compressive sensing. Our architecture employs a neural network that learns the latent sparse representations of the scene and integrates information from both the image and sparsity domains to achieve high-resolution reconstructions with high computational efficiency. A key innovation of IE-GADCI is its optimization of the incoherence between the illumination pattern and the sparse representation, which substantially improves reconstruction fidelity. We validated the performance of IE-GADCI through numerical simulations on natural and biomedical image datasets.

activity.title: Last week, I presented an ongoing project at the American Society For Mass Spectrometry (ASMS) conference: With thousands of #metabolomics papers published each year, staying up-to-date is a challenge. To tackle this, we harnessed unsupervised word embeddings using a #transformer based model to extract latent knowledge from the metabolomics literature. My presentation highlighted preliminary findings on mapping the evolution and trends within the field. Shoutout to my two undergraduate mentees at Georgia Institute of Technology School of Computing, Varun Y. and Aditya Simhadri , for their contributions to this research. Hey everyone! I am so happy and grateful to launch Weave’s beta today with Sashank and Sathwik ! In one line, Weave is an app that autodetects your screenshots and uses AI to find relevant links from screenshots and makes them actionable. Think about all screenshots you take - images of reels or TikToks of good restaurants in your area, Twitter bookmarks, products you buy or a long list of links. All these images just gather virtual dust in your Photos library! The biggest problem is that these screenshots are not actionable upon. If I had to use any of the images I stated above, I’d actually have to open a browser, type my query again and surf to get to my link. Weave seamlessly detects your screenshots from your Photos folder, filters away sensitive and private images, and contextually understands the rest to find relevant links to your images. For example, a marketplace site for a product you want to buy, the Maps/Reservation/Web link to a reel of the best mexican restaurants in NYC and so on. Please sign up for our beta here: https://www.weave.team ...more ...more

Every silicon wave follows the same law. Most people see the term GPU and forget what the G actually stands for. Graphics. It was purpose-built for exactly that workload: rendering graphics, floating point math, managing lots of cores. It was never designed for AI. It was a battlefield promotion - better than a CPU, but not what anyone would build starting from a blank sheet of paper. If you zoom out, you’ll see the same pattern has repeated across 5 decades: - 70s-80s: Personal computers. Serial single-threaded, scalar performance, standard instruction set, perfectly suited to x86. - 90s: Graphics - a new workload with highly parallel floating-point operations, created a new chip. The GPU. - 00-10s: Mobile came along. It needed low power, a small form factor and always-on connectivity. Those constraints created the opportunity for ARM - a wildly successful business for two decades. Then around 2015, we saw it again through the lens of our portfolio at Foundation Capital : statistical inference over large datasets. AI workloads that are intensely data I/O bound and were ramping very, very steeply. Whenever you see a workload spiking that hard, there's an opportunity to replace the compute layer. So you ask the first-principles question: “If you were designing for this workload from scratch, what would you build?” You'd build what we built at Cerebras . New workloads deserve custom, purpose-built silicon. That's been the story of every silicon wave for 50 years. If you want to know where the next generational chip company comes from, don't watch the chips. Watch the workloads. Thanks again for a great conversation Oz Woloshyn

Some life updates: 1) My RL drone project is complete!! I designed, built, and trained a reinforcement learning fault-tolerant octocopter from scratch with 0 prior hardware experience -- from idea to flying (non-RL) drone in 2.5 weeks (this was when I last posted about it) and idea to RL flight in < 8 weeks. Since my last post, I measured the airframe (mass, MOI via bifilar pendulum, etc), built a MuJoCo simulator, and trained the policy with PPO (asymmetric actor-critic) via PufferLib and heavy domain randomization. 20M steps later, I hand-ported the observation pipeline and network into C++ as a custom ArduPilot flight mode and motor mixer. The policy overrides AP_Motors' output stage and writes all eight motor commands directly, replacing the position controller, the attitude/rate PID cascade, and the mixer (EKF state in, motor commands out, at 50 Hz). Then, I flew the policy in real life: the drone survives all single and dual motor failures, and also survives triple and quad motor failures zero-shot, despite having never seen them before in training. One flight vid below + full build log and more details at https://lnkd.in/gwvhq-RZ 2) I attended Y Combinator Startup School, where I met so many incredible people and listened to inspiring talks from speakers like Chelsea Finn and Boris Cherny . Garry Tan and I are now mutuals on X 👾 3) I'm wrapping up my second internship with Apple in the Information Security org. Thank you so much for another incredible summer and so many lessons learned! 4) After almost 15 months away, I'm returning to Georgia Institute of Technology this August to complete the last 2 semesters of my degree. See you on campus! 🐝 📸: the drone maintaining a stable hover thanks to RL, even after I shut off 3 of its motors

A year ago, Nick , Matthew , and I were building GroundControl during YC P25. Yesterday I went back to YC Startup School as a Friend of YC. In the last year, we've grown to serve hundreds of manufacturers around the world as a team of 14. A few insights that stuck out: 1. Your brain is still the fastest chip you own. Everyone's racing to outsource thinking to AI. But for a lot of judgment calls, your own head is faster than any tool call. Round-tripping to a model for things you already know how to reason through is often slower, not faster. 2. The lean startup playbook isn't the only playbook anymore. For years, "start narrow, find your wedge" was the only reliable path. Now there are real tailwinds for going bigger, faster. We've taken that approach as we now have 4 products across GroundControl. The question isn't lean vs. ambitious but which one actually matches the moment you're building in? 3. Acceleration is exponential. 6 years ago, the top LLM user was using ~100K tokens a month. Today, the top user uses 100M+. 4. Sam Altman's quote that stuck with me: He expects the next 6 months of model progress to feel as big as the last 2 years combined. If that's even directionally right, most roadmaps are already out of date. It was exciting to meet a new wave of builders! We’re hiring, DM me.

Everyone says AI is going to kill SaaS. We're betting it rebuilds it. Today we're announcing Ergo 's $2.8M seed, led by FundersClub . We now manage over $3B in pipeline for revenue teams. With participation from Y Combinator , Georgia Institute of Technology , Coughdrop Capital , Kulveer Taggar , and many more. Every revenue team runs on conversations: cold calls, meetings, emails, Slack threads, in person meetings, and more. That's where the real signal lives, and today it's scattered across a dozen tools, and most of it goes nowhere. Ergo is the revenue infrastructure layer for AI-native GTM teams. We capture every conversation, turn it into a unified data layer, and run agents on top for follow-ups, CRM automations, coaching, forecasting, reporting — so reps spend less time on manual admin, no deals slip through the cracks, and leaders get a pipeline they can actually trust. Teams like Rho , Corgi , Retell , Agency Cybersecurity , Greptile , Sully.ai , and more already run on Ergo . The next generation of GTM won't be built on software designed for humans doing manual entry. It'll be built on infrastructure designed for agents and humans to move forward together. Thank you to our investors, customers, and the team who got us here. We're just getting started, and did a full brand refresh. Come see what Ergo can do, website linked in the comment section!
